transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick off and priya will do the demo, marcus is on for any deep infra Qs. good to see you all.
[00:18] Sam: hey alex, thanks, yeah we mainly wanted to see the embeddings + rerank flow, we run elastic + a custom tf based ranker today, latency's pretty variable at peak.
[00:35] Jin: and to add, our main worry is quality at 95%+ relevance for top 5, anything that degrades that is a no-go. also we have strict SSO + audit requirements.
[00:50] Alex: great, we'll focus on that. quick qual: what's your current qps and avg doc size?
[01:05] Karen: today we peak at ~700 qps on search, 2-3k documents per query on some internal indexes, but typical result set is 100-200 docs, we do an expensive tf-idf + neural rerank as a second step.
[01:25] Priya: got it. so conceptually with redwood hosted you'd use our embeddings endpoint to vectorize content, store vectors in your vector db (we showed pinecone earlier) or you can use a managed vector layer, then on query you do a vector recall + then call our rerank endpoint to reorder candidates — or call generation for explanation.
[01:45] Sam: can you show the actual call flow? sample code?
[02:00] Priya: yeah sure i'll share the console and a quick curl flow.
[02:15] [screen share starts] Priya: ok here's the console, top-left is the model catalog, we're using rwd-embed-medium for embeddings and rwd-rerank-2 for the rerank demo; note these are compatibility names, sometimes transcriptions see them as redwood something.
[02:35] Priya: step 1: embeddings upsert, we batch content into 512-token chunks. step 2: vector recall with cosine. step 3: rerank call where we pass top-K documents plus query, redwood rerank returns scores and a reordered list. i have a live sample next.
[02:55] [00:03:10] Marcus: quick infra note, the rerank path keeps KV cache warm for short lived contexts, but for rerank we send full doc snippets, caching isn't as critical as generation workloads.
[03:20] Priya: demo time. i'll run a sample query: 'best laptop for data scientists' against nova sample index.
[03:35] [03:40] Priya: curl call: POST /v1/rerank with body {query, candidates:[{id, text}], model:rwd-rerank-2, top_k:5} — response in ~120 ms for this small set.
[03:55] Priya: note that in hosted we see typical rerank latency ~80-250ms depending on batch size and model.
[04:10] Sam: that's promising. how does batching affect latency vs cost?
[04:25] Priya: good Q. small batches (1-8) give lowest p99 latency but higher per-query cost. larger batches amortize fixed overhead and reduce $/query but increase tail latency. redwood optimize suggests batch sizes based on your SLA.
[04:45] Jin: you mentioned prefix caching earlier for generation — does that help rerank at all?
[05:00] Marcus: not really, rerank is stateless per query since we pass candidates. caching helps when you have repeated prefix or identical queries where embeddings can be cached; the platform supports prefix/KV caching for gen flows, and vector caching in the cache layer helps recall.
[05:20] Priya: i'm going to run a slightly bigger test — 50 candidates and show the delta.
[05:35] [05:45] Priya: sending request... response took 410ms here, ordering improved significantly in top 5 compared to tf-idf baseline.
[06:00] Sam: are you using any re-ranking prompts or is it pure supervised scoring?
[06:15] Priya: rwd-rerank-2 is a learned reranker that scores candidate pairs; we also support instruction-based re-ranking (prompting) if you want explainable signals. mixing both is common.
[06:35] Jin: what about model versioning and rollouts? we need canary and A/B.
[06:50] Alex: redwood supports pinned model versions, canary rollouts, and route-based policies so you can send x% to new model and fallback on error. console shows rollout UI and metrics.
[07:10] Karen: security: SOC2, SSO, KMS — how does hosted handle customer data residency?
[07:25] Alex: hosted stores embeddings and logs in our cloud region. we have region pins for EU/US, and for strict data residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. we do KMS integration and can ingest customer keys for encryption at rest. we'll send the SOC2 and security whitepaper after.
[07:45] Jin: do you retain raw text or only vectors?
[07:55] Priya: retention depends on config; by default transient logs for 30 days for debugging but you can opt-out or set zero retention, enterprise customers often use Dedicated with no raw retention.
[08:10] Sam: latency SLOs? p95, p99?
[08:20] Marcus: for hosted rerank using rwd-rerank-2 we usually see p95 ~200ms for small batches, p99 ~450ms — but that varies by model and concurrency. Dedicated gives more predictable p99s as you control pools.
[08:40] [08:50] Priya: switching back to code — here's a sample Node flow: call embeddings endpoint, upsert to vector store, on query do recall then hit rerank endpoint, then optionally call a generate endpoint for summary/explain.
[09:05] Priya: i'll paste a quick example to chat. also linking the benchmark sheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/nova-demo (placeholder).
[09:20] Sam: good. question on costs — what's rough $/query?
[09:30] Alex: rough ballpark hosted: embeddings small model $0.0008/vec, rerank model $0.002 - depends on tokens and model; we'll send the pricing sheet with expected $/query for your qps.
[09:50] Jin: vendor lock-in? if we start on hosted and later move to dedicated or private, how seamless is it?
[10:05] Marcus: that's a core design — same API and model names across hosted, dedicated, private. you can pin versions and route to on-prem. migration requires data movement of vectors, but the API layer is consistent.
[10:30] [10:40] Karen: can we see an end-to-end demo with their dataset?
[10:50] Alex: absolutely — the POC week would allow us to ingest a sample chunk, run 10k queries, and provide latency/cost numbers.
[11:05] Sam: security again — SSO integration timeline?
[11:15] Alex: SSO (SAML/OIDC) is straightforward; we'll coordinate with your IAM — typical setup takes 2-3 business days for hosted.
[11:30] Priya: switching to a technical deep dive slide: tokenization differences can affect embeddings; for long docs we chunk, and Redwood Optimize recommends chunk size and quantization profile.
[11:50] Jin: quantization? will that impact rerank accuracy?
[12:05] Priya: quantization is applied mainly to reduce memory/cost on Dedicated; for rerank we recommend FP16/8-bit quantization profiles that preserve quality — optimize runs a few evals to pick best profile.
[12:25] [12:40] Marcus: another notable item: in high throughput scenarios we suggest hybrid retrieval (ANN recall + filtered candidate pipelines) to control recall latency.
[12:55] Sam: do you have examples where rerank actually reduced false positives?
[13:10] Priya: yes, in a product catalog example rerank improved top-3 relevance by 12% vs pure vector recall; we have before/after spreadsheets in the deck.
[13:30] Jin: what about explainability — can rerank return reasons?
[13:45] Priya: we can return scores and token-level attributions in some models, and you can also call a small explain generation model to produce human readable rationale.
[14:05] Karen: let's talk integration timeline — our holiday freeze is mid-december, can the POC start before freeze?
[14:18] Alex: we can kick off an ingest and baseline this week, but full 1-week loaded POC is best the week of Dec 13. we'll aim to get the fast parts done before your freeze.
[14:35] Sam: what metrics will you provide at the end of the POC?
[14:45] Alex: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), cost per query, recall/precision for top-K vs baseline, error logs, and a recommended config (batching, quant, model).
[15:00] [15:10] Jin: ok sounds good. any legal/procurement red flags?
[15:20] Alex: for hosted there is a standard agreement; for enterprise Dedicated we do custom terms. procurement usually asks for data processing addendum and security package — we'll include that.
[15:35] Priya: quick note: if you want to test embeddings-only first we can give a small free credit to index a subset.
[15:46] Sam: that helps. also can you confirm the retention settings options?
[15:55] Alex: yes — default 30-day logs, opt-out or zero retention possible, Dedicated can be configured with no raw retention and KMS keys. we'll include exact steps in the security doc.
[16:10] Priya: i'm going to run the scripted 10k recall + rerank test offline and share numbers — that's the action item.
[16:25] Sam: perfect. thanks everyone.
[16:35] Alex: recap: alex sends pricing + contract template, priya runs 10k bench and shares spreadsheet, jin provides sample dataset and qps. schedule POC week of 2026-12-13.
[16:55] Karen: thanks all, that was useful.
[17:05] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up in the chat with links and docs. bye.
